questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of his latest video (September 2023), he's still a fan of Blundstones, but he's retiring his own 585s to cut down his boot collection, not because he's gone off them.

**Late 2023 (Sept)**
- He says the Blundstones are "just incredible" and that he's "a big fan" who has "always loved them" [1].
- His worn-in 585s, the subject of his first video, "held up through it all" and stayed "probably my most water resistant boots" [2]. He's retiring them anyway [3].
- He's also letting go of his heavy-duty Blundstone Extreme work boots. He had thought they were waterproof, but they're only very water resistant nubuck [4].
- He talks about boots he can "flop on really quick" for errands or rain, groups Blundstones in with them, and says he's keeping them but "could easily put them on the sell list" [5].

**Earlier views**
- **2022:** He wrote that he loves Blundstones and that they're "still some of my favorites". He added that they're not as repairable as good year welted boots like Red Wings or Wolverines [6].
- **2020 (one-year review):** He called them decent for work but "not anything incredible", and a good fit for casual wear [7]. He said he'd pick a smoother leather over the distressed nubuck if buying again [8].
- **2019:** He recommended them "100%" if you'll keep them treated [9].

His opinion has been steady and positive over the years, with caveats about work use, repairability and the nubuck.

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
He thinks Solovair is the better buy. In his 2022 Dr. Martens video he calls Solovair cheaper and better built than Made in England Docs. His 2023 follow-up doesn't mention Solovair, but it repeats that the England boots are mainly for big Dr. Martens fans.

**Where Solovair wins (2022)**
- **Price:** Solovair boots are cheaper than the Made in England Docs. [1]
- **Comfort:** Solovairs have a shank, so he says they're more comfortable over long periods. Standard Dr. Martens have none. [2]
- **Resoling:** They're Goodyear welted in a more regularly accepted way, so they're easier to resole. [2]
- **Overall:** For the equivalent eight-eyed derby boot, he sums it up as "cheaper better quality better features." He also notes Solovair is one of the original makers of the original Docs. [2][3]

**Where they're about even**
He says the Made in England leather will age fine and is probably on par with Solovair. The better midsoles are probably on par too. [4]

**When he'd still pick the England Docs**
- If the yellow stitching matters to you, he says you have to get the Made in England Docs. Solovair doesn't do it. [5]
- In 2023 he says that on pure value the extra $90 over the Thailand pair is "probably not" worth it. [6]
- He adds that the England boots are for mega fans who want something close to how old Docs were made. [7]

**Caveat on Solovair**
His own Solovair pair had problems after eight wears: a back tab ripped off and a lace snapped. He assumed it was a manufacturing defect and had contacted them. [8]

hybrid.answer:
He prefers the 1907 if you're choosing between the two Red Wing moc toes. The 875 is a Goodyear-welted boot, while the 1907 adds a storm welt, a removable leather footbed and leather laces for about $10 more. In a later video (2022) he says his favorite Red Wings are actually the 3335s, over both of these.

**His verdict (2021)**
- He calls the 1907 "red wings best heritage boots by far" and says you should get it if you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing [1].

**Construction**
- The 875 is Goodyear welted. He calls Goodyear welts "really durable" and "pretty water resistant" [2]. The welt leaves room for cork that molds to your foot, and he says that's what Red Wing's cork insoles are [2].
- The 1907 has the storm welt. He says the popular view (from Reddit) is that Red Wing just stitches another strip of leather onto the welt. He adds that he's not quite sure [3]. He still calls the storm welt "invaluable" [4].

**Price and extras**
- The 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875, but he argues it isn't really more expensive [5].
- You get the removable leather footbed, which he says typically costs $40 separately, plus leather laces [4]. The footbed can also be pulled out so the boots dry faster [4].

**Soles**
- Both use crepe soles. He says he doesn't really like them [6]. In 2022 he says they break down faster than the 3335's Vibram mini lug sole [7].

**Waterproofing**
- He only tested the 1907, not the 875. One boot leaked almost immediately through the stitching. He still has "no doubt" they'd hold up in rain, grass or mud [8].

**Later view (2022)**
- He calls both the 1907 and 875 "more beefily constructed" than the 3335, so they suit you better if you need a tough boot [9].

questions.question: October is almost over, any updates on the V3 versions of the Iron Snail denim jackets?

hybrid.answer:
The Iron Snail hasn't covered a V3 version of the Iron Snail denim jackets in the videos available here, so there's no update to report.

The closest thing is the Mammoth V3. In his August 2025 studio tour he said it was "coming out later this year in black, in blue, and buffalo plaid" [1]. He added that the sample on camera wasn't final: "That is not the final mammoth. We changed a lot of stuff about it." He said the sampling fabrics weren't the real fabric and the finished jacket looks "very, very different" [2]. He doesn't call the Mammoth a denim jacket, and nothing here says whether it has been released.
